findings.problem: current-contract.md CON-DOC-004's published signature is `fetchDocuments(checkId, requestNumber, serviceCode, versionNumber)` — it has no `deadline` parameter — yet the contract's own Notes line says 'The call honours the Check's timeout (REQ-DOC-040)', and current-backend-execution-plan.md line 212 declares the real signature as `fetchDocuments(checkId, requestNumber, serviceCode, versionNumber, deadline)`. Every one of the ~61 backend test cases that exercise fetchDocuments (current-backend-test-plan.md) also cite the 5-parameter form. The contract — the stable outbound promise CHK is meant to code against — does not match what CHK must actually call to get timeout behaviour (REQ-DOC-040, AIAS-7).
findings.fix: Update CON-DOC-004 in current-contract.md to `fetchDocuments(checkId, requestNumber, serviceCode, versionNumber, deadline) → list of Document Outcome {...}`, and add a one-line note that `deadline` is how the caller conveys the Check's remaining time (REQ-DOC-040).

findings.problem: P1 adversarial probe: no artifact states what happens when `handOverUpload` (CON-DOC-003) is called for a checkId for which `endCheck` (CON-DOC-005) has already run — e.g. a late or retried INT call racing the Check's own end. The backend plan only addresses the reverse race ('a handover racing with endCheck ... is refused by the caller's Check state' — current-backend-execution-plan.md line 226) and assumes the caller (CHK/INT) never lets a handover arrive after the Check has ended. If that assumption is ever violated, the resulting Uploaded Document is never deleted: ADR-DOC-008 removes retention-purge logic precisely because 'every Check ends ... so no upload outlives its Check through DOC' — a row created after the one end-of-Check notice for that id has no second deletion trigger and persists indefinitely, which is a silent violation of POL-DOC-015 ('discard them when their Check ends') and raw-idea §12 guardrail 9. No statement anywhere in the analysis addresses this counter-case and no test case covers it.
findings.fix: Either (a) have the contract explicitly state the ordering guarantee the caller must uphold (CON-DOC-003/CON-DOC-005: 'the caller guarantees no handOverUpload call for a Check arrives after its endCheck call'), and record that obligation as a CAT-10 platform finding against CHK/INT's design (see G7), or (b) add a defensive rule (e.g. RULE-DOC-009) so handOverUpload rejects an upload for a checkId it has already received an end-of-Check notice for. Recommended: (a) plus (b) as a safety net, since DOC cannot verify Check state on its own (tier 1, no read of RPT/CHK).

findings.problem: P2 closure probe: nothing bounds how many Uploaded Documents may be handed over for one Check in `manual` mode. RULE-DOC-003 only rejects an upload with no checkId/documentType/empty file; there is no maximum-upload-count rule, so a buggy or malicious INT caller could hand over an unbounded number of documents for a single Check, growing DOC_UPLOADED_DOC (with BLOB content) without limit. The platform declares per-Check limits for timeout, rows and file size (AIAS-7) but names no cap on upload count, which is the one guardrail-8 limit raw-idea §12 does not explicitly enumerate but the spirit ('each check has limits') implies.
findings.fix: Add a configurable per-Check upload-count limit (e.g. `aias.check.max-uploads`) enforced by a new RULE-DOC-009 at handover time, with a rejection code analogous to RULE-DOC-003's; propose the limit value as a best-practice default (e.g. one per required document type, or a small fixed cap) since no owner value exists yet.

findings.problem: governance-shared/analysis/platform/project-registry.md §8 still lists OQ-1 and OQ-2 as OPEN (lines 234-235), but current-platform-summary.md's own 'RESOLVED DECISIONS (this phase)' table (decisions #1 and #2) states both are already settled — RPT owns the Check run record and the Check Document record, not DOC — explicitly citing 'project-registry §8 OQ-1' and 'OQ-2' as the rows being closed. The registry was never updated to reflect this, leaving a live artifact (project-registry.md) inconsistent with a decision the DOC analysis itself relied on (ADR-DOC-002, ADR-DOC-003, module-registry AUTO-DECISION #1).
findings.fix: Update project-registry.md §8 rows OQ-1 and OQ-2 to Status RESOLVED, with Resolution text pointing to platform-summary decisions #1/#2 and ADR-REG-001; this is bookkeeping the orchestrator can apply mechanically on gate completion.

findings.problem: Per shared/REGISTRY-SCHEMA.md §4 (CAT-10 platform findings), a module-scoped stage that discovers an obligation on another module's surface must record it in the project registry so the owning module's own gate can find it — recording one is never a reason to lower a score, not recording one is. DOC's own ADRs name at least five such obligations in prose only, each phrased 'recorded for the X analysis', but none appears as a row anywhere in project-registry.md §10 (which holds only the P-1 BOOTSTRAP/extraction events): (1) ADR-DOC-001 — CHK must not duplicate the `blob` document source query; (2) ADR-DOC-006 — INT must pass the Check's service code and version number with every upload; (3) ADR-DOC-008 — CHK must send the end-of-Check notice on every ending path; (4) ADR-DOC-010 — RPT's P2 must put the CHECK constraints for DOCUMENT_READ_STATUS/UNREADABLE_REASON on its own columns; (5) ADR-DOC-012 — INT's backend plan must list DOC's four in-process error codes in its own catalog. None of these is DOC's to settle, yet each currently depends on whoever analyses INT/CHK/RPT happening to re-read DOC's ADR text — exactly the 'not mine to settle, into the void' failure CAT-10 exists to prevent.
findings.fix: File each of the five obligations above as an OPEN CAT-10 row in project-registry.md §10 (module DOC, stage as cited, owner INT/CHK/RPT as applicable, status OPEN), before the AMEND pipeline reaches those modules' own analysis gates.
